notes: Every value traces to a cached API response (source + fetched_at per metric) or a labelled assumption in src/assumptions.yaml.

M1_intents_gross_fees.definition: USD fees/day from DefiLlama totalDataChart; 30d trailing sum
M1_intents_gross_fees.anomaly_flag: 24h fee is far below the 7d daily average ($16,604 vs $206,697/day). The last daily point in the series is the same low figure, so this is a full-day value, not a partial day — either a real one-day drop or a DefiLlama reporting lag. Never annualise a single day; 7d/30d trailing figures used throughout.

M2_intents_fee_growth.definition: 30d trailing vs prior 30d; log-regression CAGR on trailing-30d sums
M2_intents_fee_growth.trailing_30d_vs_prior_30d_reading: Fees are volatile, not a smooth ramp: trailing-30d peaked at $8,236,902 and is now -29.5% below that peak, but still above a year ago. The DCF base growth assumption (10%) is a forward assumption, NOT a trend extrapolation.
M2_intents_fee_growth.log_regression_cagr_full_series_warning: Dominated by the May-Aug 2025 launch ramp from $1/day; do NOT quote as a steady-state growth rate.

M3_retained_revenue.capture_source: revenue.near.org SSR payload (net revenue $ / gross fees $, cross-checked vs per-mechanism split) — MEASURED, not assumed

M4_capture_rate_trend.definition: Retained / gross by window (sum of three mechanisms: direct fees pp_fe + B2B pp_b2b + quote improvement pp_qi)
M4_capture_rate_trend.trend_reading: Capture is rising: all-time ~19% -> YTD ~23% -> 30D ~33%. The 30D rate, not the lifetime rate, is the base case.

M6_buyback_vs_issuance.definition: Annualised retained revenue / price = NEAR bought/yr; vs issuance = max_inflation * total_supply
M6_buyback_vs_issuance.break_even_note: NEAR turns net-deflationary when retained Intents revenue reaches this level at the current price.

M9_staking_real_yield.definition: Last-epoch APY minus max inflation (real yield to stakers)

M10_validator_health.definition: Validator set size, total stake, top-10 concentration
M10_validator_health.top_10_note: Top-10 stakes from validatorFullData (top 25 returned by the API); denominator is the API totalStake (full set).

M11_price_vs_fundamentals.definition: NEAR price (CoinGecko 365d) indexed vs trailing-30d Intents fees indexed — do fees compound while price falls?

M12_daily_txns.definition: Daily transactions on NEAR (NEARBlocks /v1/charts daily series)

M13_daily_active_accounts.definition: Daily active accounts on NEAR (NEARBlocks /v1/charts daily series)

M14_new_accounts_trend.definition: New accounts per day on NEAR (NEARBlocks /v1/charts daily series)

M15_intents_daily_volume.definition: NEAR Intents daily swap VOLUME (USD) — DefiLlama summary/dexs/near-intents totalDataChart (the dexs dimension, not fees). Fees (M1) are the revenue; volume is the growth x-axis.
M15_intents_daily_volume.implied_gross_fee_rate_note: 30d Intents gross fees (M1) divided by 30d volume from the daily series — the fee rate the market actually paid. Cross-check: secondary sources quoted a ~15 bps gross fee rate; if this lands near 15 bps the two independent series agree. It is a derived ratio, not a DefiLlama field.

M16_price_vs_fees_correlation.definition: Pearson correlation of weekly log-changes (log v[d]/v[d-7]) over the last 365 days — contemporaneous co-movement only, no lead-lag, no causation
M16_price_vs_fees_correlation.method: Weekly log-changes, aligned by calendar date; pairs with a missing or non-positive value on either side are dropped.
M16_price_vs_fees_correlation.reading: Positive r means NEAR's price and Intents fees tended to move in the same direction week to week; negative would mean they diverged. Either way this is co-movement, not evidence that fees move price or vice versa.

M17_metcalfe_check.definition: Metcalfe check: log-log OLS of NEAR price on daily active accounts (NEARBlocks /v1/charts, same daily grid for both series). Primary is monthly (month-end price vs monthly mean users); daily is the robustness line. Also: market cap on users, and price on cumulative txns (PARTIAL — trend-dominated stock).
M17_metcalfe_check.method: log(price) = a + b*log(users); strict Metcalfe predicts b ≈ 2.0. Monthly aggregates: month-end price, monthly mean active accounts, month-end market cap, month-end cumulative txns (summed over the full daily series). Rows with price <= 0 or users <= 0 are dropped before taking logs.

rival_reported.note: As reported by that entry (rival watch 2026-11-11); not independently verified. Its activity definition differs from this series, so the two slopes are not directly comparable point-for-point — the shared conclusion (disconnect) is what matters.

dropped_rows.note: All dropped rows are pre-launch Jul-Oct 2020 (price was 0 before mainnet trading; the 11 zero-user rows sit inside that window). No in-window day is dropped.

M17_metcalfe_check.partial_final_month_note: The last month covers only the days present in the series (2026-11: 1-9 Nov 2026); its mean uses those days only.

price_vs_cumulative_txns_monthly.partial_note: Cumulative txns is a monotonically increasing stock, so this regression is trend-dominated by construction; it tests whether price tracks cumulative usage, not a Metcalfe law. Reported for completeness, not as evidence.

M17_metcalfe_check.reading: On the full 74-month window the Metcalfe relation is absent: log(price) on log(users) has slope 0.0216 (SE 0.0376) and R² 0.0045 — statistically indistinguishable from zero, against the strict-Metcalfe slope of 2.0. The daily regression agrees (slope 0.0112, R² 0.0012, n=2221). Even the most favourable reading — market cap on users — gives slope 0.1859 and R² 0.2704, far below 2.0. Price does not track cumulative usage either (slope -0.0122, R² 0.0021, partial check). One caveat, reported not buried: from Jan 2024 onwards the monthly slope is 0.3275 with r 0.6393 — price and users have moved together more in the recent window, driven by the joint fall from the Apr 2024 activity peak. The relation flips sign across sub-periods (2020-2023 slope ≈ 0), so it is not a stable law. Net: value NEAR on fees, not on users — the fee thesis stands on its own numbers, and the user-count story cannot rescue the $3.60 price.

revenue_dashboard_all_time.headline_revenue_window: UNLABELLED in page payload (consistent with all-time net revenue)

snapshot.buyback_wallet_balance_vs_dashboard_note: Live NEARBlocks balance vs the dashboard's all-time traced inflow to buybacks.multisignature.near (1,771,956.8 NEAR). The live balance is HIGHER than the traced inflow, so the dashboard wallet table is partial (or stale) and must not be read as the full buyback total — the wallet also receives other inflows and spends on buybacks.

M8_valuation_multiples.definition: Market-cap / annualised-fees for NEAR (gross + retained) vs SOL/AVAX/ETH chain fees; NEAR TVL from DefiLlama series
M8_valuation_multiples.peer_fee_methodology_note: Peer chain fees are DefiLlama summary/fees 30d totals, annualised — the same methodology for all four chains, but DefiLlama chain-fee totals can undercount vs other methodologies (e.g. Solana's total here is far below figures that include all validator/Jito revenue). Use for relative ranking within this dataset, not as absolute revenue.

dropped_benchmarks.reason: DefiLlama slug returned no fee totals (404 / not found)

M18_dated_predictions.definition: The 7 committed predictions (PREDICTIONS.md, committed 2026-11-10) scored against current model outputs. Status is a point-in-time read, not the final outcome: no prediction has resolved yet (earliest resolution date 2026-12-31).
M18_dated_predictions.method: Live values are the same figures the model already computes (M₁ F₃₀, M₃ capture, base-case DCF ÷ live price, M₁₅ volume, F₃₀ ÷ Chainflip 30d fees, M₁₃ 30d-mean active accounts, |M₁₆ weekly log-change Pearson|). Thresholds are the numeric form of data/predictions.json — see PREDICTION_THRESHOLDS in src/model.py.

predictions.title: Intents fees recover to their November level
The capture rate holds its level
NEAR keeps its lead over Chainflip
The price still does not track Intents fees

M19_falsification.definition: The 6 committed falsification conditions (README.md Falsification section, committed 2026-11-11) scored against current model outputs. Status is 'triggered' only when the live value breaches the threshold AND the persistence window has been met; otherwise 'not triggered'. Persistence is counted from the commitment date: F1/F4/F6 from the stored daily series, F2 by carrying breach_since forward through this file, F3 event-based, F5 immediate by design.
M19_falsification.method: Live values are the same figures the model already computes (M1 F30, M3 capture, F30 / Chainflip 30d fees, base-case DCF / live price, F30 / M2 peak, M15 volume / prior-30d volume), except F3, whose live value is the Oct 1-4 2026 outage precedent (31.6%) cited in README Limitations. Thresholds are the numeric form of data/falsification.json — see FALSIFICATION_THRESHOLDS in src/model.py.

conditions.title: Revenue base too small
conditions.claim: The Intents toll road grosses enough fees for retained revenue to matter against a ~$4.69B market cap.
conditions.threshold: Trailing-30d Intents gross fees (F₃₀) below $2,000,000 sustained for 90 consecutive days
conditions.persistence: 90 consecutive days below threshold, counted from the commitment date (2026-11-11)
conditions.status_reason: No breach: F₃₀ $5,807,392 is above the $2,000,000 bar; 0 of 90 persistence days.
conditions.what_triggering_means: The toll-road revenue base is too small to matter: even at 100% capture, annualised retained revenue would be under $24M/yr against a ~$4.69B market cap, and the DCF case collapses to a rounding error.

conditions.title: Retention fails
conditions.claim: NEAR keeps a rising share of Intents gross fees for buybacks.
conditions.threshold: 30d capture rate (retained ÷ gross) below 15% sustained for 90 consecutive days
conditions.persistence: 90 consecutive days below threshold, counted from the commitment date (2026-11-11)
conditions.status_reason: No breach: capture 33.37% is above the 15% floor; 0 of 90 persistence days.
conditions.what_triggering_means: The retention mechanism does not work: the capture climb (19.1% all-time → 33.4% 30d) has reversed to near the all-time floor, and the DCF base case has no measured capture to stand on.

conditions.title: Concentration kills the moat
conditions.claim: Intents flow is not dependent on any single routing provider.
conditions.threshold: A single routing-provider outage cuts observed 1Click volume by more than 50% for 7+ days
conditions.persistence: 7+ consecutive days above the 50% drop bar
conditions.status_reason: Precedent only: the Oct 1–4 2026 pause ran 31.6% below the prior matching week — under the 50% bar. Event-based; re-evaluated when a new outage is reported.
conditions.source_short: NearStats routing data via Faultline; precedent: Oct 1-4 2026 service pause (README Limitations)
conditions.what_triggering_means: The moat is a single point of failure: the toll road's flow depends on one provider, and an outage at that provider is an outage of the fee base itself.

conditions.title: Competitive lead lost
conditions.claim: NEAR Intents is the toll road of its category, not one of several.
conditions.threshold: A competitor's trailing-30d Intents fees exceed NEAR's (ratio < 1.0) for 3 consecutive months
conditions.persistence: 3 consecutive calendar months with NEAR 30d fees below the competitor's, counted from the commitment date (2026-11-11)
conditions.status_reason: No breach: NEAR leads Chainflip 1.95×; 0 of 3 persistence months.
conditions.what_triggering_means: NEAR is not the toll road: another cross-chain settlement venue grosses more, and the moat claim fails on its own category's numbers.

conditions.title: Thesis too bearish (reverse falsification)
conditions.claim: Retained revenue alone supports only a fraction (~11%) of the NEAR price.
conditions.threshold: DCF value/token at or above 100% of NEAR price
conditions.persistence: None — a single recomputation at or above 100% triggers; the claim is about the current level, not a trend
conditions.status_reason: No breach: DCF value/token is 11.7% of price — far below the 100% bar.
conditions.what_triggering_means: The 'retained revenue supports only ~11%' claim was wrong in the other direction: fees or capture grew (or the price fell) enough that today's retained cash flow alone justifies the price, and the honest framing must be rewritten.

conditions.title: Growth story dies
conditions.claim: The Intents fee curve is compounding, not collapsing.
conditions.threshold: Trailing-30d fees fall more than 50% from the $8,236,902 peak of 14 Oct 2026 AND 30d volume falls more than 50% vs its prior 30d, both sustained for 90 consecutive days
conditions.persistence: 90 consecutive days with BOTH legs below their bars, counted from the commitment date (2026-11-11)
conditions.status_reason: No breach: fees are 70.5% of peak and volume 78.4% of prior 30d — neither leg is below its 50% bar; 0 of 90 persistence days.
conditions.what_triggering_means: The compounding curve is broken, not just repricing: fees and volume have both halved and stayed halved, so the DCF's growth assumption is a bet against the observed direction on both axes at once.
